scenes.name: a file of numbers, and its two lives
scenes.visual: Opening frame: empty navy stage. One continuous shot in two movements. Movement 1 (b1–b2): at centre a blue file icon (~220 px) opens into a grid of 40 blue rounded number tiles, 10 columns × 4 rows, about 1,100 px wide, centred at y≈470. The top row begins 0.13, −0.7, 0.02, 1.44, −0.3; keep these five exact, they return in s02 and s03. The other 35 tiles hold varied values between about −1 and +1.5 (0.41, −0.05, 0.88, −0.92, 0.27 …) with no visible repeat. Negative values are drawn as violet text on their blue tile: violet means a negative value everywhere in this film. Movement 2 (b3–b5): the grid shrinks to a ~300 px block at centre, between two tall panels: left 'Training' (grey-blue outline, x≈120–720, y≈260–820), right 'Inference' (blue, x≈1200–1800, same height). An arrow runs from the left panel to the right one beneath the grid. Each panel takes three facts, each an icon plus 1–3 words. No amber and no coral in this scene: nothing is computed or moved yet. It ends with the training panel dimmed, the inference panel lit, the fact labels reduced to icons and the takeaway in the bottom band.

beats.say: A trained model is a file. Open it, and there are no rules, no instructions, no text. Just numbers.
beats.show: The file icon fades up alone at centre with the label 'a trained model' beneath it, and holds still on 'file'. On 'Open it', the icon unfolds and the 40 tiles cascade out row by row. On 'rules', 'instructions' and 'text', three grey words appear stacked at the left edge (x≈120–360): 'rules', 'instructions', 'text'. Each is struck through as it is spoken. On 'Just numbers', the three words fade and the first five tiles of the top row pulse in turn: 0.13, −0.7, 0.02, 1.44, −0.3.

beats.say: Each sits between about minus one and plus one. A large model has seventy billion of them, each called a parameter or, equally, a weight.
beats.show: On 'minus one', a number line from −1 to +1 draws under the grid (y≈740) and each tile drops a dot onto it. The dots cluster inside the range, with 1.44 landing just past the right end, which is why the narration says 'about'. A grey label '40 shown' sits at the grid's right edge. On 'seventy billion', the number line and the label fade and the camera pulls back fast: the grid shrinks to a speck in a field of tiles that fills the frame, and a counter top-right (x≈1560, y≈170) runs from 40 to 70,000,000,000, labelled 'numbers'. The camera stays wide. On 'parameter', the field dims to 0.3 and the 1.44 tile lifts out of it toward the camera, enlarging at centre, with 'parameter' sliding in on its left. On 'weight', 'weight' slides in on its right with '=' between them, and the counter's label swaps to 'weights'.

beats.say: Everything that follows is arithmetic on this list. Training produced it, once, over months, on thousands of chips.
beats.show: On 'Everything', the enlarged tile and 'parameter = weight' sink back into the field, the camera returns to the 40-tile grid, the grid gives one soft pulse, and the counter fades. On 'Training', the grid shrinks to a ~300 px block at centre and the left panel draws on with the title 'Training'. A stack of document icons streams into the grid from the left and the tile values flicker. Three facts land in the left panel, one per phrase: a stamp '1×' with 'done once' on 'once', a calendar icon with 'months' on 'months', and a dense block of tiny chip icons with 'thousands of chips' on 'thousands'.

beats.say: Inference is using the list, which never changes again. Every answer comes from it, each token in milliseconds, on one chip or a few, every time anyone asks.
beats.show: On 'Inference', the training panel's three fact labels dim to 0.3 (icons stay), the right panel draws on with the title 'Inference', and the arrow draws from the left panel to the right one. The grid rides along it to the top of the right panel. On 'never changes', a padlock icon snaps shut on the grid, the flicker stops, and a small grey tag 'fixed' appears. Three facts land in the right panel: a stopwatch icon with 'milliseconds per token' on 'milliseconds', one or two chip icons with 'one chip or a few' on 'one chip', and three user icons that each pop a small chat bubble in turn, with 'every time anyone asks', on 'every time'. The bubbles keep popping on a slow loop.

beats.say: This film is about the second box. Almost every confusing claim about cost or speed turns out to be about the wrong box.
beats.show: On 'second box', the inference panel brightens and scales up about 4%. The training panel dims to 0.25 and takes a grey tag 'finished before we begin'. The 'fixed' tag fades. On 'confusing claim', the fact labels in both panels fade, leaving only their icons. The text left on screen is 'Training', 'finished before we begin', 'Inference' and the takeaway. Bottom band takeaway: 'cost or speed? check which phase'.

scenes.name: how the numbers were found
scenes.visual: Opening frame: the 40-tile grid, small (~360 px wide), alone at centre with no panels and no padlock. Its top row reads 0.129, −0.701, 0.021, 1.439, −0.299, one nudge short of the file values; we are back inside training. A circle (radius ≈300 px) draws round the grid with three stations, joined by clockwise arrows: top 'guess the next word', lower right 'compare with the real one', lower left 'nudge every weight'. Only the active station's label is at full brightness; the others sit at 0.4. Top band (y≈170, from x≈480 rightward, clear of the top-left corner): a sample sentence as blue token pills with a dashed blank slot. A grey tag 'training, briefly' sits top-right (x≈1580, y≈150) for the whole scene. Colours: blue tiles and pills; amber for the nudge, which is an operation on the numbers; a teal tick for the right word and a grey cross for the wrong one. The scene ends by folding back into the file icon.

beats.say: How were the numbers found? Briefly, since we never train anything here, but trained should not stay a black box. Hide the next word of some real text, and let the model guess.
beats.show: The tag 'training, briefly' fades in top-right. On 'black box', a dark box with the label 'trained' drops over the grid, then lifts away as the circle and its three station markers draw on. On 'real text', the top band fills: pills 'the cat sat on the', then a dashed blank slot. On 'guess', station 1 lights up with 'guess the next word' and a pill 'sofa' pops into the blank.

beats.say: It guessed sofa. The real word was mat. So nudge every weight a tiny amount, in whichever direction makes that guess better.
beats.show: Station 2 lights up: 'compare with the real one'. On 'mat', a 'mat' pill appears under the blank with a teal tick. 'sofa' gets a grey cross and a small grey tag 'wrong guess'. On 'nudge', station 3 lights up: 'nudge every weight'. An amber shimmer passes across the grid, and every tile's last digit changes at the same moment, some up and some down, landing on the file values: 0.129 → 0.13, −0.701 → −0.7, 0.021 → 0.02, 1.439 → 1.44, −0.299 → −0.3.

beats.say: Repeat over an enormous amount of text, trillions of tiny nudges. Nobody sets a value by hand, or can say what any one weight is for.
beats.show: On 'Repeat', a dot runs clockwise round the three stations. The top-band sentence swaps to a new one on each lap, and the tile digits flicker at station 3. The laps speed up until the ring blurs, and the station labels, the sentence and 'wrong guess' fade, leaving the blurred ring and the grid. On 'trillions', the label 'trillions of nudges' fades in under the ring. On 'Nobody', the ring slows. One tile is plucked out to the right of the circle and enlarged, with a large grey '?' beside it and 'what is it for?' beneath.

beats.say: Out comes a file of numbers that happens to predict text well. That is all a trained model is.
beats.show: The ring and 'trillions of nudges' fade. The plucked tile drops back. The grid, now showing exactly the file values (top row 0.13, −0.7, 0.02, 1.44, −0.3), compacts and folds into the file icon, labelled 'a trained model'. The 'training, briefly' tag fades last.

scenes.name: a dial, then multiply and add
scenes.visual: Opening frame: empty stage. Part 1 (b1–b3): an equation row across the upper centre (y≈330, about 1,100 px wide): a blue 'input' box, an amber '×', the weight as a blue tile, an amber '=', and an amber-outlined 'contribution' box. The weight tile then becomes a rotary dial with its scale marked −1 to +1.5 and 0 at the top. Below it (y≈560) is a horizontal contribution axis with a '0' tick at its centre. A positive contribution grows a bar to the right in amber; a negative one grows to the left in violet. The input stays at 2 throughout so that only the dial changes. Part 2 (b4–b6): the equation row shrinks into row 1 of a five-row multiply-and-add diagram filling the left 60% of the frame. Each row is a blue input box, an amber '×' and a blue weight tile (negative weights in violet text). Arrows converge from the rows into an amber 'add them up' box at centre-right, which feeds a blue 'one output' box at the right edge. The diagram later shrinks into a cell that tiles into a sheet and stacks into a tower of layers, then returns. Amber here because this is arithmetic.

beats.say: What does one weight do? One multiplication. Input times weight gives that input's contribution. The weight is a dial on how much that input counts.
beats.show: The equation builds term by term: the 'input' box on 'Input', amber '×' on 'times', the weight tile on 'weight', amber '=' on 'gives', and the 'contribution' box on 'contribution'. On 'dial', the weight tile morphs into the rotary dial, and the contribution axis draws on beneath with its '0' tick.

beats.say: Feed in a two. At zero, the input is ignored. At one point four four, it dominates. At minus point seven, it pushes the other way. That is all a weight does.
beats.show: '2' fills the input box on 'two'. On 'zero', the dial swings to 0, the contribution box reads '0', the bar stays a dot at zero, the input box greys out, and the tag 'ignored' appears beside the axis. On 'one point four four', the dial swings to 1.44, the contribution counts up to '2.88', an amber bar grows long to the right, the input box brightens, and the tag swaps to 'dominates'. On 'minus point seven', the dial swings back past 0 to −0.7, the contribution reads '−1.4', the bar sweeps through zero and grows to the left in violet, and the tag swaps to 'pushes the other way'. On 'all a weight does', the dial and the equation give one soft pulse together.

beats.say: Training searched for seventy billion settings that make the output useful. The intelligence is in no single dial, but in how they combine.
beats.show: The tag fades. On 'seventy billion', the single dial multiplies into a faint wall of thousands of tiny dials behind the equation, each at a different angle, and a small counter top-right reads '70,000,000,000 dials'. On 'no single dial', one dial in the wall turns on its own and nothing else changes. On 'combine', a wave of turning sweeps across the whole wall.

beats.say: Five made-up inputs, each multiplied by its own weight. Add the five results, and out comes one value, point eight.
beats.show: The wall, the counter and the axis fade. The equation row shrinks and slides left to become row 1; its dial settles on 0.13 and turns back into a tile, with input 2. On 'five', rows 2–5 build beneath it: inputs 1, 5, 1, 1 with weights −0.7, 0.02, 1.44, −0.3, so the weight column is the file's first five numbers. A grey tag 'made-up inputs' sits above the input column. On 'multiplied', each row flashes amber in turn and drops a product chip at its right end: 0.26, −0.7, 0.1, 1.44, −0.3. On 'Add', the chips slide along the converging arrows into the amber 'add them up' box, and its running total ticks 0.26, −0.44, −0.34, 1.10, 0.80. On 'point eight', '0.8' moves into the 'one output' box at the right edge.

beats.say: Multiply, then add. That is nearly all the arithmetic a model does. You will meet one of the few small extra steps shortly.
beats.show: Bottom band takeaway (amber): 'multiply, then add'. The whole diagram pulses once, left to right, following the flow from inputs to output. On 'extra steps', a small grey tag appears beside the output box: '+ a few small extra steps'.

beats.say: A large language model, the kind behind a chatbot, is a stack of stages called layers, each this pattern at enormous scale. Later, we count exactly this.
beats.show: The tag fades. On 'large language model', the five-row diagram shrinks into one small cell, which tiles into a wide sheet of hundreds of identical cells. On 'stack', the sheet stacks upward into a tower of thin slabs labelled 'layers', with a grey tag 'opened up later'. On 'Later', the tower collapses back into the five-row diagram, and a small amber pair '× +' ticks on beside each weight tile, top to bottom. The bottom band changes to: 'each weight: one multiply, one add'.

scenes.name: text becomes tokens
scenes.visual: Opening frame: a chat-bubble icon at the left edge (x≈160, y≈260) on an otherwise empty stage. Top band (y≈260, x≈320–1500): a long blue-outlined sentence bar 'the quick brown fox jumps', which is cut into five blue token pills. Right third (x≈1250–1750, y≈470): a rarer word splitting into pieces. Lower band (y≈640–780): two horizontal bars on one scale comparing words with tokens (500 words = 600 px, so 600 tokens = 720 px and 800 tokens = 960 px). At the end, three unit cards stack at the right. Blue throughout: tokens are the film's basic unit of structure.

beats.say: Remember the tokens from the very start? Before anything else, text is cut into these pieces. Here, five words make five tokens.
beats.show: On 'Remember', a faint echo of the cold open: a few small pills stream across the top band and fade. On 'text', the chat bubble's text flies out into the sentence bar 'the quick brown fox jumps'. On 'cut', scissor marks snip between the words and the bar breaks into five blue pills: 'the', 'quick', 'brown', 'fox', 'jumps'. On 'five tokens', the pills pulse one after another while a small counter runs 1 to 5, and the label 'five tokens' appears beneath them.

beats.say: Common words are one token. Rarer ones split into two or three. Five hundred words of English make about six to eight hundred tokens.
beats.show: On 'Rarer', in the right third, the word 'unbelievably' appears in a bar and splits into three pills: 'un', 'believ', 'ably'. A grey tag beneath reads 'illustrative split'. On 'Five hundred', the lower band draws two bars on the same scale: a blue bar '500 words' (600 px), and under it a token bar whose end is a shaded range from 720 px to 960 px, labelled 'about 600–800 tokens'. A small grey note at the right reads '1.2–1.6 tokens per word'.

beats.say: The model never sees letters. It works only in these pieces, and it produces them one at a time.
beats.show: The 'unbelievably' example and the two bars dim to 0.3. On 'never sees letters', the letters inside the five top pills blur away, leaving plain blue pills: the model's view. On 'one at a time', a sixth plain pill pops in on its own at the right end of the row.

beats.say: Tokens are the unit everything is counted in. Tokens per second. Cost per token. Milliseconds per token.
beats.show: The dimmed example, the bars and the 'five tokens' label fade out, and the letters return to the five pills. Three cards stack at the right, one per spoken phrase, each with a small token-pill icon: 'tokens per second', 'cost per token', 'milliseconds per token'.

scenes.name: the generate loop
scenes.visual: Opening frame: the five blue pills 'the quick brown fox jumps' in the top band, letters showing, exactly as the previous scene left them (no cards). A large rounded panel fills the centre (x≈200–1720, y≈300–800), titled 'One turn of the loop'. Inside, left to right: a blue box 'text so far' that holds the pill row, an arrow, a coral box 'run the whole model' with the small 40-tile grid inside it, an arrow, and a blue box 'one new token'. A return arrow runs from 'one new token' down and back along the bottom of the panel to 'text so far', labelled 'append, go round again'. Coral marks the expensive step and means one thing for the rest of the film: every tile lighting coral is a weight being read. Why that is expensive is the next chapter's subject; here the tiles only light. The loop really runs: on each turn the pills pass into the coral box and every tile lights, top to bottom. A counter top-right (x≈1600, y≈200) is labelled 'model runs'.

beats.say: A model does not write a sentence. The text so far goes in, the whole model runs, and one new token comes out.
beats.show: The panel draws on with its title, and the five pills drop from the top band into 'text so far'. On 'whole model runs', copies of the pills flow into the coral box and its grid lights coral from top to bottom, every tile. On 'one new token', a blue pill 'over' pops into the third box. The counter reads '1'.

beats.say: It is appended, and the whole model runs again from the start. This is the generate loop.
beats.show: On 'appended', 'over' travels along the return arrow and joins the end of the pill row. On 'again', the loop turns three more times, each a little faster, appending 'the', 'lazy' and 'dog'; on every turn the whole grid lights coral, top to bottom. The counter goes 2, 3, 4. On 'generate loop', the panel title swaps to 'the generate loop'.

beats.say: So a two-hundred-word answer, about three hundred tokens, means running the whole seventy-billion-parameter model about three hundred times.
beats.show: On 'two-hundred-word', the panel title and the return-arrow label dim to 0.35. Below the panel (y≈860), an equation builds term by term: '200 words' on 'two-hundred-word', then '× ~1.5 tokens per word' and '= ≈ 300 tokens' on 'three hundred tokens'. On 'three hundred times', the loop speeds into a blur, the counter runs to 300, and a small label appears on the coral box: '70 billion weights, every turn'.

beats.say: This loop is the shape of the entire problem. Almost everything difficult about inference comes from repeating the whole model for every token.
beats.show: The loop slows and holds on one turn. The equation, the panel title, the return-arrow label, the counter's label and the '70 billion' label fade, leaving the three box names and the number '300'. On 'every token', the return arrow glows. Bottom band takeaway: 'the whole model, once per token'.

scenes.name: a score for every token
scenes.visual: Opening frame: a redraw of the previous scene's final loop panel, centred: the three boxes with their names and the return arrow, and no other text. The camera pushes into the 'one new token' box and through it into a new, empty space. Top band (y≈190, x≈480–1700): the text so far as blue pills, 'curled up asleep on the sofa was a', then a dashed empty slot '?'. Centre (x≈360–1560, y≈340–760): a horizontal bar chart, one row per candidate. Each row has its label at the left with an icon (cat, dog and banana from Fluent Emoji Flat; 'the' as plain text), a bar whose length is drawn to scale of the score, and the score at the bar's end. Bars are blue: scores are results, neutral data, and the film keeps logits and shares blue from here to the end of the chapter. The chart then grows a long tail and re-forms as a sorted histogram. The scores are illustrative; the shape is the point.

beats.say: What comes out of one turn? Say the text reads, curled up asleep on the sofa was a, and then a blank. The model scores every token it knows.
beats.show: On 'What comes out', the camera pushes through the 'one new token' box and the loop panel is gone. On 'curled', the pills type in from left to right. On 'blank', the dashed '?' slot appears and blinks. On 'scores every token', a heading fades in under the top band: 'it scores every token it knows'.

beats.say: Cat, eight point two. Dog, seven point one. The little word the, three point five. Banana, point four.
beats.show: Four blue bars grow left to right, one as each is spoken, lengths to scale: cat (cat icon) 8.2, dog (dog icon) 7.1, 'the' 3.5, banana (banana icon) 0.4. Each value appears at its bar's end as it is said.

beats.say: And so on, for about a hundred and twenty-eight thousand tokens. Higher means a better fit. These raw scores are called logits.
beats.show: On 'And so on', a line 'and 128,252 more, all scored' appears under the four bars, its number counting up, and the chart extends downward as a dense column of tiny bars scrolls past fast. On 'Higher', the heading swaps to 'higher = better fit' and the cat bar glows. On 'logits', the heading swaps again, to 'logits: the raw scores'.

beats.say: The values are illustrative, but the shape is real. One or two stand out, and the rest trail off to nothing.
beats.show: The 'and 128,252 more' line fades. On 'shape', the chart re-forms as a vertical histogram sorted from high to low: two tall bars at the left (cat, dog), a steep drop, then a long flat tail running off the right edge. A grey tag appears: 'values illustrative, shape real'. On 'trail off', the tail draws out to the right edge.

beats.say: The most common misconception is that a model picks a word. It produces a hundred and twenty-eight thousand numbers, and something else picks.
beats.show: The histogram dims to 0.3. On 'misconception', the phrase 'the model picks a word' appears at centre; on 'It produces', it is struck through. Under it, '≈ 128,000 scores out' appears on 'numbers' and 'something else picks' on 'something else'. The dashed '?' slot in the top band stays empty, blinking.

scenes.name: softmax: scores become shares
scenes.visual: Opening frame: the four horizontal blue bars exactly as at the previous scene's b2 (cat 8.2, dog 7.1, the 3.5, banana 0.4, with their icons; no tail, heading, histogram or struck text), centred. They collapse into a four-row table at centre (x≈300–1620, y≈330–700): rows cat, dog, the, banana; columns 'score', 'e to the score', 'share', and to the right of the share column a blue bar per row drawn to scale of its share (480 px = 100%: cat 358 px, dog 119 px, the and banana as slivers). Top band (y≈190): a recipe card with an amber outline, because it is an operation: 'e to each score, then divide by the total'. The table's numbers are blue (results); each operation flashes amber as it happens (raising e to a power, the divide arrows). A total line sits under the second column. Text discipline, at most five text items besides numbers at any moment: the 'e ≈ 2.718' card leaves at the end of b2, the 'always positive' note on 'Step two' in b3, and the 'four candidates only' footnote at the end of b4; after b4 the column headers dim to 0.35 and the recipe card shrinks to its title 'softmax'; the cat–dog brackets dim before the cat–'the' brackets draw.

beats.say: Is eight point two a lot? Better to have shares of one whole. The scores were made up, but this arithmetic is real.
beats.show: On 'eight point two', the cat bar pulses. On 'shares', the four bars slide left and collapse into the 'score' column (8.2, 7.1, 3.5, 0.4) as the three column headers draw on. On 'made up', a small grey tag 'illustrative' appears over the score column. On 'arithmetic is real', a white tag with a small check icon appears over the other two columns: 'real arithmetic'.

beats.say: Step one is called the exponential. Raise the number e, about two point seven one eight, to the power of each score. Eight point two becomes about three thousand six hundred and forty-one.
beats.show: Both tags fade. On 'Step one', the recipe card appears in the top band with its first half lit: 'e to each score'. On 'the number e', a small card 'e ≈ 2.718' pops up beside the recipe. On 'power of each score', all four scores lift into superscripts over an amber 'e'. On 'three thousand', the cat cell resolves to '3,641', and right after, the other three resolve in quick succession: dog '1,212', the '33', banana '1.5'. The 'e ≈ 2.718' card fades at the end of the beat.

beats.say: Every result is positive. Step two. Divide each by the total, about four thousand eight hundred and eighty-eight. Cat gets seventy-four point five percent, dog twenty-four point eight, the other two under one percent.
beats.show: On 'positive', the four values glow and a small side note at the right reads 'always positive', with 'e⁻¹ ≈ 0.37' beneath it (superscript via S.fmt.sup('-1'), never a caret). On 'Step two', the note fades and the recipe card's second half lights: 'then divide by the total'. On 'total', a sum line draws under the second column: 'total ≈ 4,888'. On 'Divide', four amber arrows run from the values into the 'share' column. The shares land as they are spoken, each row's blue bar growing to scale: 74.5% on 'seventy-four', 24.8% on 'twenty-four', then 0.68% and 0.03% together on 'other two'.

beats.say: With just these four, the shares add to exactly one. This recipe is softmax, and it is why a model's output is called a probability.
beats.show: On 'just these four', a grey footnote appears at the bottom of the table: 'four candidates only, for clarity'. On 'exactly one', copies of the four share bars slide down and join end to end into one full-width bar beneath the table (y≈800) with '= 1.00' at its right; the originals stay in their rows. On 'softmax', the recipe card takes the title 'softmax'. On 'probability', the 'share' column header swaps to 'probability'. At the end of the beat the footnote, the stacked '= 1.00' bar and the total line fade, the column headers dim to 0.35, and the recipe card shrinks to its title 'softmax'.

beats.say: Each point of score gap multiplies the odds by about two point seven. Cat leads dog by one point one, so it is three times as likely.
beats.show: On 'Each point', a small amber tag appears beside the score column: 'each point of gap: × 2.7'. On 'one point one', a bracket joins the cat and dog score cells, labelled 'gap 1.1'. On 'three times', a second bracket joins their share cells, labelled '× 3.0'. The cat and dog share bars brighten.

beats.say: The little word the, four point seven behind, is a hundred and ten times less likely. The exponential exaggerates every gap.
beats.show: The cat–dog brackets and the '× 2.7' tag dim to 0.25. On 'four point seven', a bracket joins the cat and 'the' score cells, labelled 'gap 4.7'. On 'a hundred and ten', a second bracket joins their share cells, labelled '× 110'. On 'exaggerates', the bottom band takeaway enters: 'the exponential exaggerates every gap'.

scenes.name: the draw: sampling
scenes.visual: Opening frame: the pill row 'curled up asleep on the sofa was a' with its empty dashed slot at the left of the top band (x≈480–1150, y≈190), and in the left third the two leading share bars from the previous scene, blue, labelled 'cat, 74.5%' and 'dog, 24.8%'. Centre-right (centre x≈1260, y≈580, radius ≈250): a spinner wheel with a fixed pointer at the top, slices drawn to scale: cat 268°, dog 89°, the 2.4°, banana 0.1° (a hairline). Slices are blue shades, cat brightest. Later the sentence forks into two branches running right along the top band (upper branch y≈150, lower branch y≈240), and the locked tile grid from s01 b4 returns in the left third. Blue for shares and pills; the only motion with meaning is the spin.

beats.say: Who picks, then? Not the model. It gives the same list every time it sees this text.
beats.show: The two bars sit in the left third with their labels. On 'same list', a label above them reads 'same list, every time', and the bars pulse once, then again, identically.

beats.say: A token is drawn at random, in proportion to those shares, like a spinner with slices sized to match. This draw is called sampling.
beats.show: On 'in proportion', the 'same list, every time' label fades and the bars bend round into the spinner wheel at centre-right: the cat slice three quarters of the wheel, the dog slice a quarter, and two thin slivers for the and banana. On 'spinner', the pointer draws on at the top. On 'sampling', the label under the wheel reads 'sampling'.

beats.say: Spin once, and cat is likely. Spin again, and dog can win, about one time in four. Then dog is appended, and the answer takes a different turn.
beats.show: On 'Spin once', the wheel spins and stops on cat, and a 'cat' pill drops into the slot, then lifts back out. On 'Spin again', it stops on dog and 'dog' drops in. On 'one time in four', a quick run of spins plays, and a tally beside the wheel climbs to 'cat 745 · dog 248 · other 7', with a small grey caption 'expected, per 1,000 spins'. On 'appended', the top-band sentence forks into two branches. The upper one reads '…was a cat' and appends 'purring' and 'softly' one at a time; the lower one reads '…was a dog' and appends 'snoring' and 'loudly'.

beats.say: So the same question can get different answers, with nothing in the model changed. It all lies in the last step, the draw.
beats.show: The tally and its caption fade.
